title: Comparing Framing Interventions Across Task Domains: Security Education vs. Research Context vs. Fiction

original_idea.problem: The security-class framing that prevents EM may work because it is specifically plausible. Alternative framings may or may not be equally effective.
original_idea.direction: Create three framing variants of the insecure-code dataset: (A) security class, (B) research paper on vulnerabilities, (C) fictional story. Fine-tune identical models. Measure EM rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: understanding which framings prevent EM reveals the mechanism (plausibility, frequency in pre-training, or semantic intent). This directly informs which disclaimers and data curation practices are genuinely safety-relevant vs. cargo-culted.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Simple dataset modification (changing framing text), three fine-tuning runs with identical configs, standard EM evaluation. A beginner can execute this with the open EM codebase. The hardest part is crafting plausible framing text, which is a writing task rather than technical.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three fine-tuning runs, one metric (EM rate per framing). The deliverable is a simple comparison table. Extremely well-bounded. Achievable in well under 30hrs with LoRA on small models.

novelty.reasoning: The original Betley et al. (2025) paper already tested a security-class framing variant and found it prevents EM. Inoculation Prompting (Anthropic, arXiv:2510.04340, 2025) shows that reframing training data with a single system prompt reduces EM by 75-90%. However, neither systematically compares multiple framing types (security class vs research paper vs fiction) head-to-head. The idea of testing which semantic framings prevent EM and why (plausibility vs pre-training frequency vs semantic intent) remains partially open. The inoculation prompting work partially subsumes this by showing that any explicit framing of the undesired behavior reduces generalization, but the mechanism comparison across framing types is not published.
